3.0.s.en: 1. He punishes them because they are His people:

3.0.0.en: 1 Hear this word that the LORD hath spoken against you, O children of Israel, against the whole family which I brought up from the land of Egypt, saying, 2 "You only have I known of all the families of the earth: therefore I will punish you for all your iniquities." [1-2.]

3.0.1.en: By this introduction God, as it were, summons them to His court, declaring that He is the competent authority. He calls all the people, as the whole family that went down to Egypt and was delivered from there; He knew it by name, cared for it and called it by His name, apart from all the other families of the earth. This love and this care do not mean that He closes His eyes to their faults; rather, they place upon them all the more responsibility, for He does not accept fellowship with guilty people. He knew them and they knew Him, for it is said, "In Judah is God known" (Ps 76:1). Therefore their responsibility is greater, as the Lord says: "And that servant, which knew his lord's will, and prepared not himself, neither did according to his will, shall be beaten with many stripes. But he that knew not, and did commit things worthy of stripes, shall be beaten with few stripes. For unto whomsoever much is given, of him shall be much required: and to whom men have committed much, of him they will ask the more" (Lk 12:47-48). The more our knowledge of God's will, His mysteries and the works of His surpassing love increases, the more is demanded of us, and our responsibility before Him is greater than that of others. As St. Cyril the Great says: [The crime is not a matter for discussion in the case of one who knew his master's will and neglects it, and does not do what is fitting, although it is his duty to do so.]

3.1.s.en: 2. He does not punish without cause:

3.1.0.en: 3 Can two walk together, except they be agreed? 4 Will a lion roar in the forest, when he hath no prey? will a young lion cry out of his den, if he have taken nothing? 5 Can a bird fall in a snare upon the earth, where no gin is for him? shall one take up a snare from the earth, and have taken nothing at all? 6 Shall a trumpet be blown in the city, and the people not be afraid? shall there be evil in a city, and the LORD hath not done it? 7 Surely the Lord GOD will do nothing, but he revealeth his secret unto his servants the prophets. 8 The lion hath roared, who will not fear? the Lord GOD hath spoken, who can but prophesy?

3.1.1.en: Since God has brought His people to trial before Him, because He is the competent authority, He is like a lion roaring, a sign that they deserve judgment, for God does not seek to try His people without cause. The Lord has set out the proof through seven questions that reveal that there is no room for God to be angry without cause... and that at the same time, as He judges, He enters into a shared conversation with them, explaining to them the secrets of His trial, for "he revealeth his secret unto his servants the prophets" [7.]

3.1.3.en: "Can two walk together, except they be agreed?!

3.1.4.en: Will a lion roar in the forest, when he hath no prey?!

3.1.5.en: Will a young lion cry out of his den, if he have taken nothing?!

3.1.6.en: Can a bird fall in a snare upon the earth, where no gin is for him?!

3.1.7.en: Shall one take up a snare from the earth, and have taken nothing at all?!

3.1.8.en: Shall a trumpet be blown in the city, and the people not be afraid?!

3.1.9.en: Shall there be evil in a city, and the LORD hath not done it?!" [3-6.]

3.1.10.en: If all the answers to the preceding questions are negative, He continues in the same manner: "Surely the Lord GOD will do nothing, but he revealeth his secret unto his servants the prophets. The lion hath roared, who will not fear?! The Lord GOD hath spoken, who can but prophesy?!" [7-8.]

3.1.11.en: This speech has revealed that the trial that is taking place is not an imaginary matter but a serious and grave one, a reality that is fulfilled not without causes, but because the measure has overflowed concerning what the people committed against the Holy One and against themselves. These seven examples revealed important and grave aspects touching God's relationship with His people, because of which the trial takes place, the most important of which are:

3.1.12.en: First: The need for a new covenant, for He opens His speech by saying: "Can two walk together, except they be agreed" (or unless there is between them an appointment and an agreement)?! Certainly not! How then can God and man walk together, when the people of God have broken the covenant and violated the agreement?! The Lord says: "And if ye will not be reformed by me by these things, but will walk contrary unto me; Then will I also walk contrary unto you, and will punish you yet seven times for your sins" (Lev 26:23-24). If the people violate the covenant, how can God walk with them?! For this reason the need became urgent to establish a new covenant in which God is reconciled with His people.

3.1.13.en: This is what the Lord declared by the prophet Jeremiah: "Behold, the days come, saith the LORD, that I will make a new covenant with the house of Israel, and with the house of Judah: Not according to the covenant that I made with their fathers in the day that I took them by the hand to bring them out of the land of Egypt; which my covenant they brake, and I rejected them, saith the LORD: But this shall be the covenant... I will put my law in their inward parts, and write it in their hearts; and will be their God, and they shall be my people" (Jer 31:31-33). This was fulfilled on Covenant Thursday, when the Lord Christ gave us His Body, given for us, as a new covenant, in which we meet with the Father by our union with Him in His Son Jesus the Crucified. We enjoy the Body broken for us and the Blood shed for our salvation as a new covenant, in which our sonship to the Father is established, and His fatherhood to us, by our union in the Body of His only-begotten Son! Truly, in Christ Jesus the Sacrifice we meet with the Father and walk together, for we have agreed together in the mind of His Son and His eternal covenant.

3.1.14.en: Second: God declares that in the trial He knows no slackness. In His justice He leaves us to the evil that we have acquired for ourselves by our freedom, so that He is like the lion that roars in the forest, where rugged and fruitless humanity, like a dry desert, has become prey to be devoured. And He is like the young lion that seizes the prey offered to it to take a portion of it... We have become prey, and there is no escape from the roaring of the lion and the cry of the young lion except by taking refuge in the Cross, to see the Lion that comes out of Judah roaring not against us but against our sins, not to devour us but to crush the devil our enemy! Let us flee from the divine wrath that roars because of our accepting the enemy, by fleeing to God our Savior, who redeems us from this enemy!

3.1.15.en: Third: When He presents to us the example of the bird that falls because of the presence of a snare, or the snare that is taken up because it has caught a bird, the Lord is declaring that in the trial we are like the bird fallen in a snare. Can we save ourselves?! By the Lord our Redeemer we say: "Surely he shall deliver thee from the snare of the fowler, and from the noisome pestilence" (Ps 91:3). "Our soul is escaped as a bird out of the snare of the fowlers: the snare is broken, and we are escaped. Our help is in the name of the LORD, who made heaven and earth" (Ps 124:7-8). St. Jerome says: [What is the snare that was broken? The Apostle says: "(The Lord) shall bruise Satan under your feet shortly" (Rom 16:20), "that you may recover yourselves out of the snare of the devil" (2 Tim 2:26). You see that Satan is the fowler, who longs to catch our souls for destruction. Satan is the master of many snares and deceptions of every kind... But when we are in a state of grace our souls are safe, whereas as soon as we play with sin our souls are troubled and become like a ship beaten by the waves.] He also says: [Just as the Lord casts the net and catches a great number of fish, and His disciples, like fishermen, gather through themselves those who accept faith in Him and bring them to Him, so also the devil has his demons subject to him, who set nets for men and lead them to him.]

3.1.16.en: St. Augustine presents to us the secret of our escaping from the snare: [Because the Lord is in the soul itself, therefore the soul escaped thus like a bird from the snare of the fowlers... Let the Lord be within you, and He will save you from greater threats, from the snare of the fowlers... The snare will be broken, be sure of this, for the pleasures of the present life will not last when their final destiny is fulfilled. Therefore let us not be entangled by them, so that when the snare is broken we may rejoice, saying: The snare is broken, and we are escaped. And lest you think that you can do this by your own strength, look at who works for your deliverance and say: "Our help is in the name of the LORD, who made heaven and earth"...]

3.1.17.en: Fourth: He says: "Shall a trumpet be blown in the city, and the people not be afraid?!" It is a state of constant spiritual warfare! As long as we are in the world, the enemy does not cease to oppose us until he seizes us from the Kingdom of God into the kingdom of his darkness. Therefore the Lord sends His servants to blow constantly the trumpet of the Gospel until the final victory is achieved. The Apostle Paul says: "Finally, my brethren, be strong in the Lord, and in the power of his might. Put on the whole armour of God, that ye may be able to stand against the wiles of the devil. For we wrestle not against flesh and blood, but against principalities, against powers, against the rulers of the darkness of this world, against spiritual wickedness in high places" (Eph 6:10-12).

3.1.18.en: St. Augustine says: [Let us look at two enemies: the enemy whom we see and the enemy whom we do not see. The man we see; Satan we do not see. Let us love the man and beware of Satan. Let us pray for the man, and let us pray against Satan.] He gives the reason for this: "For when we suffer from the men who trouble us, it is only because they are vessels of Satan; he uses them and inflames them as vessels that he moves for his own account."

3.1.19.en: Fifth: The Lord declares that He is the One who permits the trial for the sake of chastisement. "Shall there be evil (calamity) in a city, and the LORD hath not done it?!" The Fathers spoke much about the word "evil" occurring here or in similar expressions, distinguishing between two kinds of evil: the evil that is evil by its nature and contrary to virtue or goodness, and the evil that is pain or distress that we ourselves consider evil. This is what St. John Chrysostom affirmed in more than one place, and as Father John of Damascus says: [He does not mean by these words that God is the cause of evil, but that the word "evil" is used in two ways, with two meanings. Sometimes it means what is evil by nature, which is contrary to virtue and contrary to the will of God, and sometimes it means what is evil and distress to our feeling, that is, sorrows and calamities. These seem evil because they are painful, though in truth they are good, for to those who understand they are a whistle (alarm) calling to conversion and salvation. Of these the Scripture says that "God is their source."] As Father Theodore says: [When the divine judgment speaks with men, it speaks with them according to their human language and feelings. The physician cuts or cauterizes those who suffer from sores for the sake of the soundness of their health, and yet those who are unable to endure it see it as evil.]

3.1.20.en: Sixth: God declares that if He is the One who permits the chastisement, He "revealeth his secret unto his servants the prophets." This is what we see in all the books of the prophets, that God does not deal in a dictatorial manner, commanding and forbidding, but reveals His secrets and reasons with them. For this reason He often repeats Himself in His speeches, because of man's weakness, so that he may grasp the unfathomable mysteries and God's high purposes as far as man is able to receive them.

3.1.21.en: God loves man and speaks with him as one equal to another. When He wanted to burn Sodom and Gomorrah, He said: "Shall I hide from Abraham that thing which I do?" (Gen 18:17). And He gave Abraham the opportunity to converse about Sodom and Gomorrah, until Abraham said to Him: "Wilt thou also destroy the righteous with the wicked?... Shall not the Judge of all the earth do right?" (Gen 18:23-25). The Lord was not angry with him, but continued the conversation as though he were His friend and equal!! And in more than one place He declares, "Come now, and let us reason together, saith the LORD"... He wants conversation with man in order to reveal His secret to the upright who fear Him. For it is said: "His secret is with the righteous" (Prov 3:32), "The secret of the LORD is with them that fear him; and he will shew them his covenant" (Ps 25:14).

3.2.0.en: Seventh: Finally the Lord reproaches them: "The lion hath roared, who will not fear? the Lord GOD hath spoken, who can but prophesy?" [8]. If God in His love reveals His secret to His prophets, how is it that they in turn do not announce to the people the roaring of the Lion who came out of His tribe, so that they may fear Him, and His words, so that all may prepare to meet Him? The work of the prophets is to deliver the divine message, even if it appears like a burning fire or a roaring lion, so that all may fear and return to God... The goal of all this is that the prophets utter prophecies as a preparatory way for the coming of the Lord.

3.2.1.en: St. Augustine has a delightful comment on the saying "The lion hath roared, who will not fear?" He says: [Man has been able to tame the lion, so that he does not fear lions once they are tamed, but he cannot tame himself; let him hand himself over to God alone, the tamer of souls. Are you stronger than the lion? For you are in the image of God! What? Can the image of God (that is, man) tame wild beasts, and God cannot tame His image?!] Then let us put our souls in His hands, for He alone is able to tame them.

3.3.s.en: 3. He calls the Gentiles to witness against them:

3.3.0.en: 9 Publish in the palaces at Ashdod, and in the palaces in the land of Egypt, and say, "Assemble yourselves upon the mountains of Samaria, and behold the great tumults in the midst thereof, and the oppressed in the midst thereof. 10 For they know not to do right, saith the LORD, who store up violence and robbery in their palaces. 11 Therefore thus saith the Lord GOD; An adversary there shall be even round about the land; and he shall bring down thy strength from thee, and thy palaces shall be spoiled."

3.3.1.en: God wanted their pagan neighbors to bear witness against them: the rich of Ashdod in Philistia (in the Septuagint, Assyria) and the rich of Egypt, the near and the far, to come and witness the seat of judgment. It is as though God found no righteous men among His people to judge between Him and His vineyard, so He resorted to strangers to judge whether there is any injustice in God's judgment toward His people. Perhaps by calling them He also wished that they would come into contact with Him and perceive His holiness and so take warning, for if He judges His people for their sins, would He show partiality toward those who are not His people?! In their presence there is an opportunity for them to review themselves also.

3.3.2.en: The hideousness of the sins within Samaria, the capital of Israel, has reached not only the holy God, so that He cannot bear it, but even the Gentiles, who bear witness against them for their evil... because the smell of evil has reached them. What bitterness! Instead of the sons of the Kingdom bearing witness against the wicked and condemning them, the wicked have become witnesses against the people of God, seeing in their midst great tumult and confusion instead of the heavenly life of surpassing glory, and within it oppressions instead of justice and righteousness. They turned into storehouses of injustice and robbery, so that they could not do right. The Lord says to the Gentiles about His people: "Assemble yourselves upon the mountains of Samaria, and behold the great tumults in the midst thereof, and the oppressed in the midst thereof. For they know not to do right... who store up violence and robbery in their palaces" [9-10.] Therefore He besieges it with distress from every side and removes from it its strength and authority!

3.3.3.en: Israel had become like the salt that should have seasoned others, but now that it has become corrupt, with what shall it be salted? "It is thenceforth good for nothing, but to be cast out, and to be trodden under foot of men" (Mt 5:13). In God's eyes Israel was like the high priest who intercedes for the pagan nations; if he sins, who will intercede for him?! It befitted Israel to be the teacher of the Gentiles about salvation, but since it left the faith, what shall its reward be?

3.3.4.en: All this terrifies the Christian, especially the priest, for the wider our responsibility, the more severe the punishment when we sin. St. John Chrysostom says: [If others fall, perhaps they can obtain pardon, but if the teacher falls, he is without excuse and falls under an extremely harsh vengeance.]

3.4.0.en: 12 Thus saith the LORD; "As the shepherd taketh out of the mouth of the lion two legs, or a piece of an ear; so shall the children of Israel be taken out that dwell in Samaria in the corner of a bed, and in Damascus in a couch. 13 Hear ye, and testify in the house of Jacob, saith the Lord GOD, the God of hosts, 14 That in the day that I shall visit the transgressions of Israel upon him I will also visit the altars of Bethel: and the horns of the altar shall be cut off, and fall to the ground. 15 And I will smite the winter house with the summer house; and the houses of ivory shall perish, and the great houses shall have an end, saith the LORD."

3.4.1.en: God has presented a wonderful simile in His chastisement of His people. Although He is the Shepherd who seeks every straying sheep and snatches it from the mouth of the lion, even if nothing remains of it but two legs or even a piece of its ear... this surpassing care and wonderful love is also what makes Him search for His people wherever they are, to allow them to go into captivity for the sake of chastisement.

3.4.2.en: The feelings of many Fathers were stirred before the surpassing pastoral love of God, so that St. Basil said in one of his letters: [Strive to rise from the ground, and remember that you have the Good Shepherd who follows your track and saves you even if nothing remains of you but two legs or a piece of an ear, bringing it out of the mouth of the beast that wounded you. Remember God's mercies, for He heals you with oil and wine. Do not despair of salvation.]

3.4.3.en: The Lord, who by His love snatches us from the mouth of the lion, is the One who snatches the Israelites from their land, whoever they are, "that dwell in Samaria in the corner of a bed" [12.] And He follows their track even if they flee to Damascus, even in bed; from there He draws them to the land of captivity.

3.4.4.en: He punishes not for the sake of punishment in itself, but for two things: the removal of idol worship, "I will also visit the altars of Bethel: and the horns of the altar shall be cut off, and fall to the ground," and the shattering of the life of luxury and pampering, of those who bought special houses for summer and others for winter, and built for themselves great and costly houses of ivory!
